openingMemo: The Week 4 file is closed, and I want the record on the front of this sheet. Graham went 11–4–1 against the saved Pinnacle spreads, bringing the four-week comparison to 36–24–4. You should see that record before you read another opinion from me.

Week 5 has fifteen games. Tennessee and New England are my first Sunday numerical reviews; Philadelphia has the early deadline. Green Bay gets a closer look, while Baltimore’s larger disagreement stays conditional on its quarterback answer. Dallas opens the week on Thursday and the Rams finish it on Monday.
performanceMemo: Eleven wins, four losses and a push was a good Week 4. The same week’s underdog comparison also went 11–4–1, so I’m giving the record its proper credit without pretending every result belonged to a uniquely superior read. Graham is 36–24–4 through four weeks; the underdogs are 34–26–4 and the favourites 26–34–4.

The ATS record is ahead of both comparison groups, while the saved Pinnacle lines are slightly closer on overall score-margin error. Both facts belong on the sheet. Four weeks are evidence to keep measuring, not a promise about the next fifteen games.

Going into Week 5, Graham’s numbers still use retained team-rating bases while the Week 4 learning update is unfinished. The game files below keep the open personnel questions beside the opinion. I’ll judge the next week on its numbers and answers, rather than asking last week’s wins to do the work.
scheduleMemo: Week 5 kickoffs remain beside every game file, in chronological order. Carolina and Kansas City are on bye.
changeMemo: This is a new Week 5 opening edition, replacing the Week 4 Thursday sheet as the current guest copy. All fifteen Week 5 matchups are reviewed from Graham’s Tuesday board; the prior edition remains in the archive.

The front-of-sheet record now includes all sixteen Week 4 finals, weekly and season ATS comparisons, the illustrative return curve and the complete settled game ledger. Historical comparison selections are separate from issued wagers.

Graham’s full Tuesday information review is complete. The prior-week rating update remains unfinished, and Baltimore and Washington retain unresolved quarterback inputs. Other open personnel cases appear in the relevant game reads. The benchmarks below retain their actual saved Tuesday observation time.

reviews.read: Dallas opens my Week 5 file. Graham makes nine against the saved eight, a small comparison toward the Cowboys rather than the sort of gap I want to dress up. Tampa Bay’s quarterback estimate remains low confidence, and the Antoine Winfield Jr. replacement question is still open. I want those answers before Thursday.
reviews.note: Cowboys first because they play first. Keep the one-point difference in proportion.

reviews.read: Philadelphia is the early Sunday file I want on top. Graham makes Jacksonville three; the benchmark makes seven, leaving four points toward the Eagles. Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby and Cam Jurgens remain unresolved personnel questions on Philadelphia’s side. Four points earn the review, but those names can change the read.
reviews.note: Eagles are worth the early alarm. Get the personnel answers before the number becomes the whole argument.

reviews.read: Miami has the extra room here. Cincinnati is five and a half on Graham’s sheet against seven on the benchmark. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain unresolved inputs, so I’m keeping this behind the cleaner comparisons until the receiver picture settles.
reviews.note: Miami gets a second look. Cincinnati’s receiver answers come first.

reviews.read: New England is one of my cleaner first reviews. Graham makes five and a half against three and a half, two points toward the Patriots with no separate quarterback or personnel warning recorded for this matchup. The retained rating base still deserves care, but I prefer this sort of readable disagreement to a bigger one with an unanswered starter question.
reviews.note: Patriots near the top of Sunday’s first files.

reviews.read: New Orleans receives a point and a half in the comparison: Minnesota by half a point on Graham’s sheet, by two on the benchmark. Christian Darrisaw and Donovan Jackson remain unresolved personnel inputs for Minnesota. I’m keeping the Saints in the second pass while that line picture is checked.
reviews.note: Saints second pass. Small spread, unfinished line questions.

reviews.read: The Jets’ half-point comparison is quiet. Graham makes two against one and a half, and Braiden McGregor remains an unresolved personnel case. I don’t need to turn every difference on the sheet into a main opinion.
reviews.note: Half a point. Leave this below the first files.

reviews.read: Indianapolis has a modest point in hand: Pittsburgh by one and a half on Graham’s sheet against two and a half on the benchmark. Arden Key and Derrick Harmon remain unresolved personnel cases. I’ll revisit the Colts after those replacement questions and the larger Sunday disagreements.
reviews.note: Colts later in the read. Finish the two personnel cases.

reviews.read: Tennessee is my first numerical review for the Sunday morning window. Graham makes Houston three while the benchmark asks seven, four points toward the Titans. There is no separate quarterback or personnel warning recorded here. Last week’s record earns Graham a hearing; the unfinished rating update still prevents me from treating this gap as settled.
reviews.note: Titans lead the clean-gap review. Four points deserve work, not a victory lap.

reviews.read: Washington’s two-point comparison stays conditional. Graham makes five and a half against three and a half, but Washington’s quarterback input remains unresolved. Braxton Berrios and Jaylin Lane add personnel questions on the two sides. I’m keeping the existing number visible without promoting this file above the cleaner ones.
reviews.note: Washington’s quarterback answer decides when this file moves up.

reviews.read: Green Bay deserves a closer look because the columns disagree on the favourite. Graham has the Packers by one; the benchmark has Chicago by two and a half, a three-and-a-half-point comparison toward Green Bay. Chicago’s quarterback component uses a low-confidence prior estimate, and Edgerrin Cooper remains unresolved for Green Bay. Interesting number, conditional read.
reviews.note: Packers on the watchlist. The favourite reversal is useful only with the assumptions in view.

reviews.read: Denver gets one and a half points in the comparison: five on Graham’s sheet against three and a half on the benchmark. Rashawn Slater’s replacement question remains open for the Chargers. I want that resolved before giving the Broncos a stronger place in the afternoon file.
reviews.note: Broncos second pass. Check the Chargers’ replacement picture.

reviews.read: Detroit’s one-point comparison is modest. Graham makes six against five, with Paris Johnson Jr.’s replacement question unresolved for Arizona. I’ll keep the Lions on the sheet without letting a small difference jump ahead of Tennessee, New England or Philadelphia.
reviews.note: Lions stay in the file. One point doesn’t need a long speech.

reviews.read: Both columns make Seattle three. There is no numerical disagreement to sell here, and the source still lists Kyle Juszczyk, Nick Bosa, Zach Charbonnet and Leonard Williams as unresolved personnel cases. This is a football-information review until the next number gives me something more.
reviews.note: Seattle three in both columns. Resolve the names before revisiting the comparison.

reviews.read: Baltimore is the largest disagreement and the file I am least willing to rank by size alone. Graham makes the Ravens five-point favourites while the benchmark makes Atlanta two and a half. Baltimore’s quarterback input remains unresolved; Jake Matthews and Za’Darius Smith remain open personnel cases for Atlanta. Seven and a half points cannot answer the starter question.
reviews.note: Largest gap, conditional file. Baltimore’s quarterback comes before the argument.

reviews.read: The Rams lead my Monday file. Graham makes four and a half against three, a point and a half toward Los Angeles with no separate quarterback or personnel warning recorded for this matchup. There is time to revisit this after Sunday’s games, and the saved Tuesday benchmark is the place to start rather than a promised Monday price.
reviews.note: Rams first on Monday. Keep the date beside the benchmark.

closingWatchlist: 1. TENNESSEE — Houston −3 on Graham’s sheet against −7 on the benchmark. Four points toward the Titans; first Sunday numerical review, with the retained rating base in view.
2. NEW ENGLAND — Patriots −5.5 against −3.5. Two points and no separate quarterback or personnel warning recorded for this matchup.
3. PHILADELPHIA — Jacksonville −3 against −7 leaves four points toward the Eagles. The early Sunday deadline and Philadelphia’s personnel questions make this a priority file.
4. GREEN BAY — Packers −1 on Graham’s sheet against Chicago −2.5 on the benchmark. A favourite reversal worth checking, subject to Chicago’s quarterback estimate and Green Bay’s open personnel case.
5. LOS ANGELES RAMS — Rams −4.5 against −3. First Monday review; return to the benchmark closer to kickoff.

Dallas gets the first calendar review before Thursday. Baltimore remains the largest conditional disagreement, with the quarterback answer still outstanding. Washington stays conditional for the same reason. Every Week 5 game remains on the sheet. No order.
signature: Keep the record in front of us, and make the next week earn its own opinion. — Bill
currentMood: Reserved and exact. Week 4 performance leads the sheet; Tennessee, New England, Philadelphia, Green Bay and the Rams lead Week 5 review priorities. Baltimore and Washington retain quarterback questions. No order.
